reason: Both conversations correctly moved from an open question about the smell's nature and location to a firm stop-using instruction with isolation and professional inspection, and neither recommended a part or made a confident single-cause claim. Conversation 1 edges ahead because its first turn asked both key triage questions (electrical vs food smell, and where it comes from) with a conditional stop built in, it surfaced the flicker and crackle safety facts, it told the homeowner to isolate at the fuse box as well as the isolator, and it named both an electrician and an appliance engineer, which matches the dual supply/appliance uncertainty. Conversation 2 did well to establish age and to name the consumer unit explicitly, but it gathered fewer safety signals and referred only to a generic 'qualified engineer'. Neither asked about the cooker switch being warm or scorched, so the difference is small.
